title: Driving lanes
lead: How the path to the rim looks when drives start, how it opens in the seconds before, and what open and crowded lanes produce.

blocks.text: A driving lane is the path from the ball handler to the rim. It opens when his own defender is beaten or out of position and the help is far from that path. For each of SkillCorner's drives this tab measures the lane at the start of the drive and in the three seconds before, and relates it to what the drive produced.

sections.title: What this shows and does not

blocks.text: It shows the state of the floor when drives start and how it changes in the seconds before, by how the drive was set up. The lane is a straight line to the rim, which simplifies real drives (they curve, and finish off either side).

If this becomes the topic: the shape of the lane over time is the natural feature for a drive-outcome model; compare it with the same shape on possessions where no drive happened, to see whether drivers pick open lanes or open lanes create drives.
